s1.where: A full-screen notification permission prompt with a bell picture and two buttons.
s1.expectation: A screen asking me to turn on notifications, before I reach the main part of the app.
s1.cue: The heading "Turn on notifications from Messenger" and the buttons "Turn on notifications" and "Not now".

first_pass.why: The heading says literally what this screen is for. There is no navigation, but it is a single question and I know what it is asking.

s2.where: The main chat list, with the bottom tabs Chats, People, Notifications.
s2.expectation: I am on the chat list, the Chats tab.
s2.cue: The word "Chats" in the bottom bar is blue and the others are grey. The large "messenger" logo at the top is only the app's name, so that did not help.

first_pass.why: The bottom bar states the current section in text and marks it with colour. That is enough. The top logo only says which app I am in, which I already knew.

s3.where: Side menu over the chat list, heading "Ally Cooper", list starting with Communities.
s3.expectation: A side menu that has slid over the chat list. I think it is the main menu.
s3.cue: The panel covers about two-thirds of the screen and I can see the chat list behind it. At the top it says "Ally Cooper", which is a person's name. I assume it is my account.

first_pass.why: The only heading is a person's name. A name does not say that this is a menu. No item in the list is marked as the current one, so I cannot tell where I came from or where I am in it.
first_pass.solution: Put a heading such as "Menu" at the top of the panel, and mark the item for the screen I am currently on.

test_cases.task: Open the side panel from Chats, read it, close with Back; open it again from People and read it again.
test_cases.real_if: The panel never names itself and never marks where you came from.
test_cases.not_real_if: Something on it tells you what it is and where you are.
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the panel from Chats. The top says "Ally Cooper" with a down arrow and a gear, then the list. There is no word like "Menu", and nothing in the list is highlighted. I closed it with Back, went to People and opened it again. It looked exactly the same, and nothing marked People as where I came from. So it is real: the panel never names itself and never shows where I was. One extra problem: my first tap after opening the panel landed on the "Ally Cooper" row, and a "Switch profile" page opened that I did not intend. I left it without changing anything.

s3.closing_comment: The panel is the same from every section and never says what it is or where I came from.

s4.where: Panel with a small "Meta" logo and a large "Subscriptions" heading, listing Facebook Plus and Meta One.
s4.expectation: The Subscriptions page, where Meta subscriptions are listed.
s4.cue: The large heading "Subscriptions" and the sentence "Find and manage your subscriptions all in one place."

first_pass.why: "Subscriptions" is a literal name for the page and the content matches it. The small "Meta" text above is a company name, but the large heading is enough.

s5.where: Blue full-screen offer with a Facebook logo, heading "Try Facebook Plus free for one week", button "Start your free week".
s5.expectation: An advert for a paid Facebook Plus subscription, opened from the subscriptions list.
s5.cue: The heading "Try Facebook Plus free for one week" and the price "$3.99/month".

first_pass.why: The heading is a sales pitch, not the name of a place. The large Facebook logo makes me think I may have left Messenger and be inside Facebook. Only the X at the top suggests I can go back.
first_pass.solution: A plain title such as "Facebook Plus subscription" at the top, and a note saying whether I am still in Messenger.

test_cases.task: Side panel > Subscriptions > second row; read the top; tap the first "View all benefits"; read the top; leave with the X on each page.
test_cases.real_if: You cannot say which part of the app these pages belong to, or cannot find the way out.
test_cases.not_real_if: You can name where you are and leave without trouble.
test_cases.what_happened: Subscriptions opened as a sheet with "Meta" at the top. Without my doing anything, that changed to "Meta Account" a moment later. The second row, Meta One, opened a page with the large words "Meta One" and "Choose your plan", which I could read as a plan selection page. "View all benefits" showed a grey loading skeleton first, then a page headed "Try Meta One Core free for one month". In the capture it said one week; now it says one month. The X at the top left was clearly visible this time. Each X took me back exactly one step: Meta One, then Subscriptions, then the chat list. I never saw the Facebook Plus page, because the try used the second row. So it is partly real. I could always leave, but the headings are product and sales words, and nothing says whether I am still in Messenger.

s5.closing_comment: I only saw the Meta One pages, not the Facebook Plus page; I could leave easily but the headings are sales words.

t132.where: First picture: the "Me" page scrolled to the Profile and Preferences settings. Second picture: a page titled "Avatar" with "Make your avatar".
t132.action_sentence: You stayed on this screen and scrolled up.
t132.expectation: The second picture says I am on the Avatar page. That is not the page I was on, and I was told I stayed on the same screen.
t132.cue: The title "Avatar" in the top bar, in the place where "Me" was.

first_pass.why: The title is clear on its own, but it contradicts the sentence. If I only scrolled up, the title should still say "Me". Instead it says "Avatar" and the list of settings is gone. Either the scroll opened the Avatar item, which I did not intend, or the title changed under me. In both cases the screen did something I did not choose.
first_pass.solution: Scrolling up should only move the list. The "Me" title should stay in the top bar, and a page should only open when I tap an item.

t132.closing_comment: Scrolling only moved the list; the "Me" title stayed and no page opened.
